text:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: KV prefix-cache cardinality spike detected in prod-east-pool for inference-runtime at 2026-03-15T14:12:01Z. Eviction rate high, OOM churn observed. Paging oncall.

maria: I'm on this. Pinging @ajay and @sasha for metrics + recent deploys.

ajay: grabbing metrics now — continuous-batching.batch_pad jumped to 1024 across many hosts, avg batch size up 3x, prefix_key_cardinality went from ~120k to ~2.4M in 10m. Evictions spiking.

sasha: any deploys around 13:58?

deploy-bot: release: inference/quantize-sampler @ 2026-03-15T13:58:12Z -> rolled to prod-east. changelist: tokenizer-normalize whitespace tweak (opt-in).

maria: ok, sounds like a combo: tokenizer change + big batch_pad = amplified prefix variants. Initiating immediate mitigations: 1) roll batching config back to stable, 2) flush affected prefix cache.

ajay: applying config rollback: POST /admin/configs/continuous-batching {"batch_pad":256,"max_tokens":512}

ops-bot: Command output:
```
POST /admin/configs/continuous-batching -> 200 OK
applied to pool prod-east (targeted hosts: 12)
previous batch_pad=1024 -> now 256
```

maria: triggering prefix cache flush for model ml-redwood-13b+ with prefix_namespace=prompt_v2_hash. Running admin-tool: `kvctl flush --model ml-redwood-13b+ --namespace prompt_v2_hash`

ops-bot: Flush output:
```
kvctl: flushing 1.9M keys from prompt_v2_hash on prod-east
flushed shards: 18/18
duration: 48s
```

ajay: eviction rate trending down immediately. CPU and mem pressure dropping on hosts that got rollback + flush. Latency p50/p90 back to baseline for most routes. p99 still elevated for some customers, investigating tail.

customer-success: FYI we have two enterprise customers (AcmeCorp, FinTechX) reporting p99 spikes ~5-10s between 14:05-14:22 UTC. CS engaged, we're drafting incident email.

sasha: looking at templating tests — I can repro different prefix keys when whitespace normalization flag toggles. Minimal repro:
```
// template snippet
promptA = "Summarize:\n  - item1\n"
promptB = "Summarize:\n- item1\n" // different leading space -> different tokenization -> different prefix hash
```
When tokenizer-normalize was toggled it changed token boundaries for many user templates; those ended up creating a new, orthogonal set of prefix keys. With large batch_pad the runtime kept caching and inflating KV namespace quickly.

maria: good catch. Immediate plan: 1) keep batching rollback (prevent re-amplification), 2) add normalization shim at prefix-hash path as a temporary safety (normalize whitespace), 3) patch tokenizer flag in next release with a migration plan.

ajay: patched canary runtime (3 hosts) to include prefix-normalize=true before hashing. Observing canary for 10m. No regrowth so far.

ops-bot: canary telemetry snapshot (10m): prefix_cardinality delta ~+0.6% vs previous window; eviction rate stable; tail errors down.

maria: rolling patch to remaining hosts in prod-east in 15m if stable. I'll keep CS updated and prepare a status note for customers.

customer-success: Notified AcmeCorp/FinTechX with ETA for resolution and mitigation steps. Both accepted mitigation and want postmortem.

sasha: longer-term fixes I propose: 1) add unit tests for tokenizer/template whitespace invariants, 2) make prefix hashing resilient to insignificant template diffs (whitespace/normalized punctuation), 3) introduce an alert when prefix_cardinality growth > 5x in 5m for any model.

ajay: ops follow-ups: tighten upper bound on continuous-batching.batch_pad in defaults (max 512), add a circuit-breaker that refuses batch_pad > 512 without canary flag. Also add telemetry for batch_pad correlated with prefix_cardinality.

maria: I'm filing INC-2026-031 on the tracker with assigned owners: sasha (RCA + tokenizer fix), ajay (runtime circuit-breaker + telemetry), maria (customer comms + postmortem).

ops-bot: Summary for incident channel:
- Impact: transient high memory/eviction + p99 latency spikes for subset of requests 14:05-14:22 UTC; two enterprise customers reported tail latency.
- Actions: rolled continuous-batching config to stable, flushed affected prefix namespace, patched prefix-hash normalization in runtime canary then rolled to pool.
- Status: mitigated, monitoring.

maria: handoff to incidents team for postmortem. I'll leave this thread open until full rollout completes and customers confirm no residual impact. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: closing note: please include timeline + code snippets and test artifacts in the postmortem.

maria: thanks team — nice fast triage. Will follow up with RCA draft in next 48h.
